rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=24, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=123, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, outer_wall_s=1700, lr=0.0001, unet_c=16, rationale=iter-14: ONE confirmation knob -> seed 42 -> 123, at the iter-13 val_n=24 PEAK basis (val_n=24/ep12/lr1e-4/warm_start=True/n_iter600/grad_clip1.0). A SECOND-SEED variance read on the NEW wider 24-scene basis (the variance of the wider-basis ceiling estimate is the one quantity iter-13 left un-pinned). This is a CONFIRMATION move, NOT a ceiling-raiser -- no ceiling-raiser remains for the over-parameterized U-Net on this 128-view synthetic substrate. DIAGNOSIS (numbers, not pixels): iter-13 val_n 12->24 (seed42) gave SSIM 0.4616, PSNR 13.45, hr 0.0011 -- landing squarely in the predicted [0.46,0.48] family, so the seed42 ceiling read is now on a 24-scene basis. But the wider basis has been read at ONLY ONE seed (42). At val_n=12 the seed spread was seed42=0.4724 / seed123=0.4484 / seed7=0.4305 (3-seed mean 0.4504, std 0.0173); whether doubling to 24 scenes shrinks that spread (the ~sqrt(2) averaging argument) is untested -- the wider-basis variance is the last un-pinned quantity in the ceiling documentation. FAILURE MODE = the 0.466 M-param U-Net OVERFITS each single noisy 128-view sparse-phantom scan (the 6-param bilateral twin physically cannot, which is why the twin clears baseline at hr+0.33 while this U-Net stays hr~0 at ~0.45-0.51 SSIM); the per-image fit has an init-driven stochastic noise floor that a wider val basis shrinks but does not eliminate. EXHAUSTED / FORBIDDEN axes (do NOT retry): n_iter (iter-2 1200 steps 0.4785->0.4293, per-scan overfit), warm_start (iter-8 off -0.0595, load-bearing-positive), lr (iter-3 1e-3->1e-4 + iter-9 1e-4->2e-4 bracket 1e-4 as optimal), pretrain_epochs (ep12 peak, ep18 worse 0.5016), unet_c (design-doc warned-against; mayo n2i c16->c32 flat), grad_clip=1.0 (LOAD-BEARING 128/2304-view FBP-adjoint overflow guard, mandatory). The ONLY genuinely-untried confirmation knob is seed AT the new val_n=24 basis. LEVER CHOICE: seed 42 -> 123 at the val_n=24 PEAK config, pairing the second seed with the wider basis to measure how much of the val_n=12 seed spread (std 0.0173) survives the doubling to 24 scenes. HYPOTHESIS: at val_n=24 the seed42 (0.4616) and seed123 reads land CLOSE (|delta| < ~0.02, tighter than the val_n=12 seed42-vs-seed123 delta of 0.024), because averaging over 24 independent per-scan draws cancels most per-scan init stochasticity -> a trustworthy ~0.46 finalized wider-basis ceiling for the per-image U-Net N2I on this synthetic 128-view substrate. hr stays ~0 (structurally FBP-bounded on dense 128-view phantoms). FALSIFIER: if the two val_n=24 seed reads STILL swing wide (|delta| > ~0.04), the stochastic floor is INTRINSIC to the per-scan N2I objective (not just init-set sampling that wider averaging would cancel) and that wide floor IS the documented ceiling finding -- the over-parameterized U-Net is structurally the wrong tool here vs the bilateral twin (hr+0.33). Either branch advances the iter-20 CEILING-DOCUMENTATION mandate. WALL: warm 12x200=2400 + per-image 24x600=14400 = 16800 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 1394 s; iter-13 ran this exact budget in 1651 s, under the outer_wall_s=1700 guard (per_scene_s = 1700/24 ~= 71 s, ample for 600 steps @ ~0.083 s/step ~= 50 s) and under the 00:30:00 (1800 s) sbatch wall. All recon-affecting knobs IDENTICAL to the iter-13 seed42 config (train_n=200, val_n=24, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=12, n_iter=600, lr=1e-4, unet_c=16, outer_wall_s=1700); ONLY seed 42 -> 123 changed.
